\title{A single motion objective for BOLD, ASL, diffusion and slow-flow MRI time series with a re-descending trajectory prior}

\section*{Synopsis}

Head-motion estimates in MRI time series absorb whatever changes the images in step with the acquisition: ASL label
alternation, diffusion contrast, eddy currents, the physiological alternation of fast BOLD. One solver registers all
frames of a series jointly with the acquisition design inside its objective, applies the terms physics calls
displacements, removes the terms physics calls contrast, and damps the head trajectory with a re-descending prior gated
on three phantoms with known motion and five clinical series. On multi-shell DWI, acquisition terms hold 73 to 83\,\% of
the phase-encode step and 39 to 62\,\% of the B0-immune readout step.

\section*{Introduction}

Single-reference registration assigns every design-locked image change to head motion [1,2]: ASL label alternation,
diffusion contrast and eddy currents, the physiological alternation of fast BOLD. Post-hoc filtering of the pose
trajectory without the acquisition design fails in both directions: an unguided phase-encode alternation filter shrinks
real head jitter (reducing true FD from 0.94 to 0.15\,mm in audit), whereas a convex trajectory prior strong enough to
remove jitter also damps slow drift and real steps. One objective registers each frame against its acquisition-level
reference under a curvature-normalised re-descending trajectory prior whose form and weight are set by a phantom and
clinical gate.

\section*{Methods}

\textbf{Forward model (Figure~1A).} Frame $k$ at reference-space point $x$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
I_k\!\big(E_k(P_k x)\big)\,\big(1 + \tilde a_k^{\top} p\big)\,\gamma_k \;\approx\; \bar I_{\ell(k)}(x),
\qquad
P_k x = R_k (x - c) + c + t_k,
\qquad
E_k y = y + p\,\big(a_{k0} + \tilde a_k^{\top}(y - c)\big),
\label{eq:model}
\end{equation}
with $P_k$ the rigid pose (rotation $R_k$, translation $t_k$) about centre $c$, $E_k$ the eddy-current affine along
phase-encode axis $p$ whose four coefficients (shift $a_{k0}$, shears and scale $\tilde a_k$) are linear in the diffusion
gradient $g_k$ via $C$, $(a_{k0}, \tilde a_k) = C g_k$ [3], $1 + \tilde a_k^{\top} p$ its Jacobian determinant, $\gamma_k$ a
spatially uniform per-frame gain for scanner drift, and $\bar I_{\ell(k)}$ the mean of level $\ell(k)$ (b-shell, label
state, encoding state). Frame $k$'s six pose parameters are $m_k + D_k \beta$: free head pose $m_k$ and design-locked
offset $D_k\beta$ (per level, with the five real $l = 2$ direction terms per shell), which is removed from the reported
pose and never applied. The acquisition design enters the default \texttt{joint} engine in $\bar I_{\ell(k)}$ and
$D_k\beta$ only (along $p$, $D_k\beta$ is restricted to the orthogonal complement of the eddy covariates so odd-in-$g_k$
displacements belong to $E_k$ and even-in-$g_k$ contrast shifts stay in $D_k\beta$). One batched optimisation over all
frames maximises Mattes mutual information against $\bar I_{\ell(k)}$, L-BFGS then a coupled full-resolution Newton
stage; each frame writes transform chain \texttt{[rigid, eddy]} (because a transform list acts on the reference-space
point $x$ first-listed first, this reproduces the fitted $E_k(P_k x)$) in one interpolation.

\textbf{Prior (Figure~1B, C).} With $u_t = m_t - \tfrac12 (m_{t-1} + m_{t+1})$ the second difference of the head
trajectory in mm at frame $t$ (rotations scaled to a 50\,mm cortical lever arm), the objective adds
\begin{equation}
\lambda \kappa \sum_t \rho\big(|u_t|\big), \qquad
\rho(u) = \frac{\delta^2}{2}\log\!\Big(1 + \frac{u^2}{\delta^2}\Big), \qquad
\rho'(u) = \frac{u}{1 + u^2/\delta^2}, \qquad \delta = 0.05\ \text{mm},\ \lambda = 0.03\ (0.05\ \text{for one-level designs}),
\label{eq:prior}
\end{equation}
with weight $\lambda$ in curvature units relative to $\kappa$, the measured curvature of the image term per mm$^2$ (median over
frames and translation axes at every stage). Normalising by $\kappa$ makes $\lambda$ dimensionless across contrasts (an
unnormalised weight of 0.02 displaced a motionless low-contrast ASL phantom by 0.1\,mm, whereas curvature scaling gives
zero). The pull $\rho'(u)$ peaks at knee $\delta$ and re-descends as $\delta^2/u$, so linear drift ($u_t = 0$) and
multi-knee steps pass while sub-knee wiggles are damped. The coupled Newton stage uses the positive-definite iteratively
reweighted least-squares majoriser $\rho'(u)/u \cdot I_6$ ($6\times 6$ identity $I_6$) per term, added once to the
image-only Hessian, because the exact Hessian $\rho''(u)$ is indefinite beyond $\delta$. Two alternatives sharing the
same knee $\delta = 0.05$\,mm and curvature-unit scale were gated: Charbonnier (quadratic below $\delta$, constant pull
above) and a steep-origin form with full pull at $u \to 0$ (\texttt{sparse}, knee $\delta/10$), testing the hypothesis
that small second differences should be shrunk hardest.

\textbf{Gate.} On three phantoms with known trajectories (ASL drift with jitter, DWI with a planted 0.4\,mm eddy shift,
slow-flow encoding states), no phantom may lose more than 10\,\% framewise displacement (FD) error against no prior and
DWI must gain; on five clinical series the B0-immune readout step median absolute deviation (MAD) must move less than
0.02\,mm, foreground temporal standard deviation (alignment) less than 1\,\% and mean FD rise less than 2\,\%.
Same-engine repeat runs on MPS agree within 0.001\,mm (0.00018\,mm maximum pose difference).

\textbf{Account.} Per acquisition axis, frame-to-frame step variance splits into head ($m_k$), applied eddy ($E_k$) and
removed design-locked ($D_k\beta$) shares; per voxel, sequential Type~I sums of squares (after removing per-frame gain
$\gamma_k$) against the design, motion regressors after design, and residual, raw and corrected. FD is computed from
$m_k$ alone; for censoring only, the near-Nyquist respiratory/cardiac alternation is removed [2,4], while the full unfiltered
poses $m_k$ are the spatial correction.

\textbf{Data.} Resting BOLD ($T = 300$ volumes, repetition time TR 1.0\,s), two ASL series (25 volumes with M0; 60
volumes without M0), two multi-shell DWI series ($b = 1500/3000$\,s/mm$^2$, 100 and 99 volumes), and an independent
four-run task-fMRI session (OpenNeuro ds007693, sub-07, ses-01, $4 \times 340 = 1360$ volumes, TR 1.5\,s); syntx 6.29.0,
antsxdwi 0.33.x, antsxfunctional 0.23.x, antsxslowflow 2.12.x.

\section*{Results}

\textbf{Gate (Figure~2).} Every prior that shrinks small second differences hardest failed: although \texttt{sparse} at
unit weight removed 71\,\% of sub-knee jitter energy on a 1-D synthetic curve (versus 54\,\% for Charbonnier; Figure~1C),
on the 3-D phantoms at weight 0.1 \texttt{sparse} raised the ASL phantom's FD error 86\,\% and slow flow's 55\,\%, and
Charbonnier raised them 70 and 50\,\%: the phantoms' sub-knee jitter is true motion planted in the trajectory. The
re-descending (\texttt{cauchy}) form at 0.03 passed every gate: phantom FD error $-14$\,\% (ASL), $-17$\,\% (DWI),
$-3$\,\% (slow flow); on the five clinical series the readout step moved at most 0.011\,mm, alignment was unchanged
($\le 0.1$\,\%), FD changed $-0.9$ to $+1.8$\,\%, and every frame converged on four series (56 to 85\,\% without the
prior; 60-volume ASL 78\,\% vs 87\,\% without; BOLD runtime 207 to 34\,s). At 0.05 the same form passed the phantoms
($-7$, $-27$, $+3$\,\%) but lowered the high-motion DWI readout step by 0.043\,mm (MAD 0.081 to 0.038\,mm) and failed the
clinical gate.

\textbf{Account (Table~1, Figure~3).} On the two DWI series, eddy holds 73 to 83\,\% of phase-encode step variance and
the removed design-locked term holds 39 to 62\,\% of B0-immune readout step variance. After correction, design explains
96.0 and 95.5\,\% of voxel variance (up from 94.4 and 90.5\,\%), motion after design falls from 1.06 to 0.67\,\% (1.1 to
0.7\,\%) and from 2.04 to 0.82\,\% (2.0 to 0.8\,\%), residual falls from 4.5 to 3.3\,\% and from 7.4 to 3.6\,\%, and the
corrected residual is uncorrelated with FD ($r = -0.02$, $-0.13$). On resting BOLD, motion variance falls from 32.94 to
20.78\,\%, and band-limited FD lowers the mean from 0.60 to 0.31\,mm and censored frames ($> 0.20$\,mm) from 46 to
13\,\%. On 25-volume ASL, design variance rises from 97.0 to 98.3\,\% and motion after design falls from 0.34 to
0.18\,\%. On the independent task-fMRI session (ds007693, four 340-volume runs, syntx 6.27.0), the Cauchy prior at 0.05
(above the 0.03 default) lowered FD on 4/4 runs (4-run mean 0.2016 to 0.1987\,mm, i.e.\ 0.202 to 0.199\,mm), kept
censored volumes ($\text{FD} > 0.50$\,mm) unchanged at 12 of 1360, and preserved whole-brain T1w-space first-level GLM
maps across all five contrasts (voxelwise $\beta$ correlation 0.9937 to 0.9989, i.e.\ 0.994 to 0.999 against no prior),
4.3 times faster end to end (2606 to 600\,s).

\section*{Discussion}

Over a third (39 to 62\,\%) of readout displacement and three quarters (73 to 83\,\%) of phase-encode displacement on
these DWI series were acquisition-locked: single-reference misattribution, measured. Our initial hypothesis failed: the
form that removes the most sub-knee jitter on a synthetic trajectory (\texttt{sparse}) is rejected by the phantoms
because their jitter is real. Amplitude shrinkage toward identity (\texttt{pose\_shrinkage} at 0.1 curvature units) also
failed: it lowered clinical FD by 11 to 41\,\% within the readout floor, but increased ASL drift-phantom FD error 2 to
3$\times$ by pulling drifting trajectories toward zero.

\textbf{Limitations.} (1) The phantom generators plant jitter in the ground-truth trajectory, not as noise in the images,
so the claim that sub-knee jitter in real data is measurement noise has no image-noise phantom gate yet. (2) On the
60-volume ASL series without M0, the design explains 1.8\,\% of voxel variance while motion after design holds 55.42\,\%,
an image-domain coupling that is not yet separated. (3) Censoring thresholds (0.20\,mm BOLD, 0.50\,mm ASL/DWI) are not
yet tied to a downstream reproducibility outcome on these five series. (4) The alternative design-in-metric engine
(\texttt{engine="projected"}) over-reports B0-immune readout jitter on real multi-shell DWI (0.145\,mm vs 0.080\,mm on
high-motion DWI, with 63\,\% of its readout translation in the span of the even-in-$g_k$ direction columns vs 4\,\% for
\texttt{joint}) and is not default. (5) True head motion that alternates at the exact period of the acquisition design
lies in the span of $D_k$ and cannot be separated from $D_k\beta$.

\section*{Novelty Assessment}

\textbf{What builds on prior work.} Mutual-information robustness to activation contrast follows Freire and Mangin [1];
the 4-parameter phase-encode eddy affine $(a_{k0}, \tilde a_k) = C g_k$ and its Jacobian modulation follow Andersson and
Sotiropoulos [3]; notching respiratory pseudomotion from censoring FD follows Power et al.\ [2] and Fair et al.\ [4].

\textbf{What is new in this contribution.}
(1) \emph{Operational partition between applied displacements and removed contrast offsets inside one multi-modal
objective:} a single solver across BOLD, ASL, multi-shell DWI, and slow-flow MRI applies physical displacements
(\texttt{[rigid, eddy]} and its Jacobian) in one interpolation while estimating and removing design-locked pose offsets
$D_k\beta$ from the reported motion without resampling them into the data.
(2) \emph{Curvature-normalised re-descending second-difference prior with IRLS Newton majorisation:} scaling $\lambda$ by
the stage-wise median translation curvature $\kappa$ makes the prior dimensionless across contrasts, while the Cauchy
influence function $\rho'(u)$ damps sub-knee ($< 0.05$\,mm) wiggles and plateau oscillations ($4.3\times$ to $6.1\times$
faster convergence) without shrinking linear drift or multi-knee head steps.
(3) \emph{Dual phantom and B0-immune readout-floor gate:} combining ground-truth drifting phantoms with the physical
constraint that regularisation must not shrink steps along the distortion-immune readout axis ($< 0.02$\,mm) falsified
amplitude shrinkage, steep-origin L1, Charbonnier, and over-weighted Cauchy ($\lambda = 0.05$).
(4) \emph{Closed-form pose and voxel variance ledger (\texttt{syntx.motion\_decomposition}):} directly quantifies the
share of step variance and voxel variance held by head motion, eddy distortion, and removed design-locked bias per
series.

\section*{Conclusion}

On these BOLD, ASL, multi-shell diffusion and slow-flow series, one objective separates head pose, eddy distortion and
design-locked offsets, reports each term's variance share, and uses the one prior setting that passed the phantom and
clinical gates together.

[1] Freire L, Mangin JF. NeuroImage 2001. [2] Power JD et al. PNAS 2019. [3] Andersson JLR, Sotiropoulos SN. NeuroImage

holds contrast and a displacement along phase encode (colorbar in signal units). (B) Surround penalty $\rho(u)$ in mm$^2$ (solid) and pull $\rho'(u)$ in mm (dashed) at
weight $\lambda = 1$ in curvature units against the second difference $u$ of the trajectory in mm (0 to 0.5\,mm; $n = 3$ forms: Cauchy, Charbonnier, \texttt{sparse}); knee
$\delta = 0.05$\,mm (dotted). The re-descending Cauchy pull peaks at the knee and fades. (C) Reconstructed trajectory (mm vs frame, $T = 80$ frames) under a
